title: Light as a circadian stimulus for architectural lighting

findings.consequent: Nocturnal melatonin production

findings.consequent: Nocturnal melatonin suppression

findings.consequent: Melatonin suppression

findings.quote: it was hypothesized that a CS value of at least 0.3 would be enough to promote entrainment in various populations, and as a result of this increased entrainment, sleep, mood and behaviour would be improved.

findings.consequent: Circadian entrainment (melatonin), sleep efficiency, self-reported sleepiness (in submariners)
findings.quote: Young et al. showed that exposing submariners to a lighting installation delivering a CS of at least 0.3, increased measures of circadian entrainment... increased sleep efficiency... and reduced self-reports of sleepiness

findings.antecedent: Summer months (average CS ~0.3) vs. winter months (average CS <0.2)
findings.consequent: Sleep duration, sleep efficiency (in office workers)
findings.quote: office workers in summer months had greater sleep duration and efficiency than in winter months.

findings.antecedent: CS greater than 0.3 in morning hours (8am-noon) vs. CS 0.15 or less
findings.consequent: Sleep onset time, sleep quality, disturbed sleep, depression (in office workers)
findings.quote: office workers who receive a CS greater than 0.3 in the morning hours fell asleep earlier, reported having better sleep quality, less disturbed sleep, and feeling less depressed.

findings.consequent: Subjective alertness
findings.quote: subjective alertness was significantly lower under a 479-nm narrowband light source than under a 437-nm and a 532-nm narrowband light source

findings.antecedent: Melanopic illuminance function vs. photopic illuminance function
findings.consequent: Fit to delta KSS values (subjective alertness)
findings.quote: When delta KSS values were plotted against a melanopic illuminance function, the fit was better than when compared to the photopic illuminance function.

findings.consequent: Prediction of acute melatonin suppression, clinical and sleep outcomes
findings.quote: the CS metric developed from the model has been shown to be predictive of acute melatonin suppression in laboratory studies and of clinical and sleep outcomes in field studies.

findings.consequent: SCN activation (without ipRGC axons)
findings.quote: neural signals from the retina reach the SCN without conduction through the ipRGC axons, but these connections are limited.

findings.consequent: Consideration of timing, duration, distribution, photic history
findings.quote: Other lighting characteristics that affect the circadian system (timing, duration, distribution and photic history) are not considered in the CS metric.

findings.consequent: Consideration of non-visual alerting effects of light
findings.quote: no consideration is given to the spectral and the absolute sensitivity of the non-visual alerting effects of light exposure.

findings.consequent: Brain activity, melatonin concentrations
findings.quote: 40 lux to 200 lux at the eye of a 640-nm (red) light has been shown to enhance brain activity during the day and night without affecting melatonin concentrations.

findings.consequent: CS calculations
findings.quote: the spectral reflectances of architectural materials must also be considered in the CS calculations

limitations: Our knowledge about the human circadian system is incomplete.
The CS metric is incomplete; other lighting characteristics that affect the circadian system (timing, duration, distribution and photic history) are not considered.
No consideration is given to the spectral and the absolute sensitivity of the non-visual alerting effects of light exposure in the CS metric.
The spectral reflectances of architectural materials must be considered in the CS calculations.
The ideas expressed are based on the authors' experience and insights and have not been vetted among the entire community of lighting stakeholders.
minimum_safe_summary: The paper argues for adopting the Circadian Stimulus (CS) metric to quantify light's effect on the human circadian system in architectural spaces. It details the CS metric's development from biophysical research, including the roles of various retinal photoreceptors and the b-y color channel, and its non-linear response to light levels. Key findings demonstrate that the CS metric better characterizes nocturnal melatonin suppression data (r²=0.91) than melanopsin-weighted irradiance (r²=0.87) and has been successfully validated in laboratory studies and real-world applications to predict melatonin suppression, circadian entrainment, and improvements in sleep, mood, and agitation. Limitations include the CS metric's current incompleteness, as it does not consider light timing, duration, distribution, photic history, or non-visual alerting effects, and the need to account for architectural material reflectances.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Light, particularly its spectral composition, intensity, timing, and duration, acts as a primary zeitgeber (time-giver) for the human circadian system, influencing physiological processes such as melatonin secretion.

mechanism_chain.description: Light absorbed by specific retinal photopigments sends signals to the central circadian clock, which then regulates the synthesis and release of melatonin.

steps.to_construct: Activation of retinal photoreceptors (e.g., intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells - ipRGCs)
Transmission of signals to the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN)
